content: For matching a discrete performance note sequence to a discrete score note sequence with wrong/missed/extra-note classification, sequence alignment via Needleman-Wunsch-style global alignment (edit distance with substitution/insertion/deletion costs) is the right tool, not raw DTW: DTW warps a continuous time axis and handles expressive timing well but does not naturally yield a discrete match/substitute/insert/delete labeling, and it mishandles repeated-note runs. Needleman-Wunsch Time Warping (NWTW) is a published hybrid that combines DTW's multi-to-one mapping with NW's gap penalty and jump handling, used specifically for performance-to-score evaluation with error costs. For this project's needs (mark each played note as correct/wrong-pitch/extra, each expected note as hit/missed, per chord-as-a-set) a cost-scored NW/edit-distance DP over onset-windowed note-or-chord tokens is the simplest correct model; reserve DTW-style time-warping for later tempo-drift/expressive-timing refinement.
